topics.topic: How Registry identifies and independently checks the agent session on Kernel's calls, and whether Kernel can claim any session
questions: Kernel holds one token for all sessions. How does Registry know which session a Kernel call is for, and what stops Kernel naming another session's id? Does Kernel ever call without a session, as itself?
Registry learns which session a call is for only from Kernel, which also registers the sessions. What makes Registry's check independent of Kernel, and does Registry trust Kernel's session claim?
The session is named by Kernel, so what makes Registry's check 'independent of Kernel' (R0-46, R0-47)? Can Kernel's token act for any registered session?

quotes: Cabinet Kernel registers each agent session with Registry; the owner sees the
read — tells it whether any project outside its set exists. Registry checks on
to the session's set; a revocation holds for flows already running at their
set, and Registry checks it again on every call, independently of Kernel, and
operations and classes the owner allows the agent, confined to the working

| read the session's access | Cabinet Kernel for one agent session; owner | the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46) | an unknown session answers that it has no access |
judgement.divergence: One Registry accepts whatever session id Kernel's single token names on each call, so Kernel can use any registered session's grants; another binds each call to a session by something Kernel alone cannot assert, and refuses a call naming a session Kernel did not prove. The owner notices which grants a compromised or faulty Kernel can reach, and Kernel notices which calls are refused.
judgement.why: The texts promise a check 'independently of Kernel' but leave unnamed whether Kernel is trusted to name the session, which is a trust boundary State 0 must name.

topics.topic: Import sources, input form, cross-instance id conflicts, and repeat or retried imports
questions: Which instances count as 'running instances' rather than test instances, given that the agent's machine is called a test instance? What is the import's input (a dump file or a live connection)? How are two source instances holding the same id (R0-21) resolved? Is a second import after the 'once' refused?

Which running instances are the sources, given that R0-50 says test-instance data is never carried over? What happens when two source instances hold the same id (R0-21)? Is there no import at all after this one migration, although R0-34 and R0-44 speak of import as a standing path?

How does the import receive the running instances' data: an uploaded export file, a direct read of their stores, or something else? Which instances are sources, given that test instance data is never carried over? Can a refused import be retried, given 'once'?

quotes: the projects of the running instances under the identities they carry
owner, confirming, once (R0-50)
any conflict with an id production holds refuses the whole import, nothing applied; an import the owner has not confirmed refused
Any conflict refuses the whole import; nothing is applied in part.
Data of test instances is never carried over automatically.
judgement.divergence: One implementation lets the owner retry an import that was refused, and takes data from every running instance; another refuses every import after the first attempt, and treats the running instances as test instances whose data is never imported. The owner notices whether the migration can be completed after a conflict, and which instances' projects reach production.
judgement.why: The texts do not say which instances are sources, given that non-production instances are test instances, nor whether a refused import consumes the 'once'; the input format, though, belongs to a later state.

topics.topic: What validate, list rooms, list artifacts and the agent projection answer for ungranted versus unknown projects without revealing existence (R0-47)
questions: R0-47 says nothing the agent receives tells it whether a project outside its set exists. For an agent, what do validate, list rooms, list artifacts and the agent projection answer for an unknown project compared with an existing but ungranted one?

What does validate answer Kernel for the agent when the project is not in the session's set? It must not reveal whether the project exists (R0-47), and the table says the answer carries every failure.
What does validate answer when Kernel asks about a project outside the session's set? R0-47 forbids revealing whether that project exists.

For an agent-authority call on a project outside the set, does the 'not found' versus 'not granted' check order reveal existence (R0-47)? Which refusal does the agent get on list rooms and list artifacts?

judgement.divergence: One Registry answers an ungranted project with a 'not granted' refusal and an unknown one with `not_found`, which reveals existence. Another answers both alike, either as `not_found` or as one indistinguishable refusal. Kernel and the agent see different answers, and the owner's no-existence-leak guarantee holds only in the second.
judgement.why: The validate, list rooms, list artifacts and agent projection rows give no failure for an ungranted project that matches R0-47, and validate's answer vocabulary has only `not_found` and `archived`.

Does 'a service' include Kernel acting for the agent on any project, against R0-41 and R0-46? Or is Kernel confined to granted projects here, as it is for 'list artifacts'?

topics.topic: Whether Kernel's publish/withdraw of artifact pointers for the agent is confined to the session's granted set, and with which refusal
questions: When Kernel publishes or withdraws a pointer on the agent's behalf, does Registry refuse a project the session is not granted, as R0-41, R0-46 and R0-47 require for every agent-authority call, and with which failure?

R0-41 has the agent publish and withdraw Kernel's pointers only on a granted project, but these rows carry no session confinement and no 'not granted' failure. Is Kernel's publish always under agent authority and confined to the session's set, or does Kernel also publish as a plain producer?

When Cabinet Kernel publishes or withdraws a pointer with agent authority, is it confined to the session's granted set (R0-41, R0-46, R0-47)? If it is, what is the refusal? Does Kernel also hold an unconfined producer authority?

Does a restriction refuse any correction of a project that already names the restricted customer, or only a correction that newly names it? R0-51 says 'no project may newly name it'.
Does `context`, or 'read a project' by a trusted service, still carry the `customer_ref` of a restricted customer? Is it marked as restricted there?

topics.topic: Trigger, observable output, failure and lawful-ground holdback for automatic retention erasure
questions: No row carries this system action. What triggers it, what does it leave observable (an audit entry, a status), how does it fail, and who records the lawful ground or purpose that holds data longer (R0-49, R0-52)?

No row carries the action Registry performs on its own when a period ends. Who triggers it, what does it output (audit entry, notice to the owner), and what is its failure, for example a lawful ground that holds the data back?

judgement.divergence: One Registry silently erases data when a period ends and lets no one record a holdback ground. Another leaves an audit entry or notice, and offers the owner an action to record the lawful ground or purpose that keeps the data longer. The owner notices whether erasures are visible and whether a holdback can be recorded at all.
judgement.why: Registry's own erasure on expiry, and the recording of a lawful ground or justified purpose, are actions the product needs, yet no row carries them with an output and a failure.

topics.topic: Access requests from unregistered sessions and pending requests superseded by a direct grant

questions: When the owner revokes the session's active project, what becomes the active project? Can 'change the active project' name a project outside the set, and what is refused for an unknown session?

topics.topic: Handling of legacy v1 data that lacks newly required fields during import
questions: v1 data has no Customer kind, no object (only a project address) and maybe `customer_ref`s without Customer records. Is such data refused, filled in during the owner's mapping check, or imported with the missing values left empty?

topics.topic: How a Capability Box receiver verifies a project reference and revision
questions: Against what does a receiver verify a project reference and revision? No Registry action returns a revision to a service (validate does not).

topics.topic: Keeping personal data in names, uris and payload_refs out of the agent projection, and their disclosure class
questions: The display name, room names and pointer uri or payload_ref may contain an address or a customer's name. How is that kept out of the agent projection, and what disclosure class do these fields carry?

topics.topic: Owner's action listing agent sessions and pending access requests
questions: No row lists the agent sessions or the pending access requests for the owner. What does that action return, and how are sessions identified to the owner?

questions: onboard_object created projects, but Kernel no longer creates projects (R0-41) and only the owner creates them. Is onboard_object still a client at all, and with which token? Which part of its role do Kernel flows take?

topics.topic: Whether the owner interface is unreachable from VM Agent
questions: Is the owner interface unreachable from VM Agent, as the service API is? Otherwise the agent could reach the owner's sign-in surface.

topics.topic: Whether the session can see an access request's state, such as a decline

topics.topic: Which services count as 'trusted services' versus 'a service'
questions: Which services count as 'trusted services'? Does Kernel without agent authority count as one? Why do some rows say 'a trusted service' and others 'a service'?
